parole.significato: an iron chain used to tie or to drag logs
parole.testo: Borrowed from Transylvanian Saxon Schivlänk, from the verb shiven (“to push, to shove”). Cognate with English shove.
Borrowed from Transylvanian Saxon Hetschenpetsch, Hetschumpetsch, Hetschepetsch, Hätschenpätsch (“rosehip”). Compare German Hetschepetsch, Hungarian hecsempecs, Hungarian csipkék (“rosehips”).
Probably from Transylvanian Saxon Piërsch (piersch, Pi^ärsch) (compare German Pfirsich), ultimately from Latin persica. Doublet of piersică.

parole.significato: young horse (up to three years old)
parole.testo: Unknown. Possibly from a Vulgar Latin root *caballānus, diminutive of Latin caballus, or from carnalis. Compare also Spanish carnero. Scriban (1939) proposes Transylvanian Saxon Jêrlänk, which is cognate to German Jährling and English yearling. Other theories include a Slavic *kъrdlanъ or a pre-Roma
